source_policy.note: Mission 041 roles are used as the working constraint frame; geometric traces are tied to photo indices rather than reopened facade classification.

P1.use: Global host envelope only; no local stair metric inferred.

P2.use: Long host side and strong grade change constrain low-level context.

P3.use: Raised timber deck, its supports, masonry stair at left, upper circulation zone and house contact are visible.

P4.use: Upper masonry platform, tall masonry faces, large lower opening/covered void, stair parapets and timber-deck adjacency are visible.

P5.use: Stair system is recut from another angle; lower and upper portions are non-collinear and the upper portion reaches the masonry platform.

observed_geometry: A real horizontal upper masonry walking surface is visible adjacent to the house.
Tall white masonry faces support/bound the upper platform.
A large dark lower opening/covered void remains visibly open under part of the masonry platform.
Solid parapet/side-wall edges accompany the exterior stair.
At least two stair portions with a direction change are required by the multi-view traces; a single straight flight does not explain P3/P4/P5 together.
The upper stair portion reaches the upper masonry platform.
The timber deck is a distinct raised system adjacent to the masonry complex and remains outside MODULE 003.
user_declared: Owner-confirmed topology: exactly two major stair runs with one turn; no metric run dimensions supplied.
Owner-confirmed descent route: from the masonry platform, one run extends beyond the rear plane, turns left, then the second run descends to the low courtyard; ascent is the reverse.
Owner-confirmed platform relation: masonry platform and timber platform are distinct walking surfaces connected by exactly one step; exact step height is unresolved.

competing_hypotheses.geometry: two major runs with one turn and an intermediate landing/turn zone
competing_hypotheses.reason: Explains the non-collinear visible stair portions, altitude gain, platform arrival and cross-view reappearance with minimum geometry.
Contradicts the distinct non-collinear stair portions and confirmed turning zone visible across P3/P4/P5.
No additional major direction change is required by the five-photo evidence; it would add unsupported geometry.

inferred_geometry.coordinate_frame: Combined viewer frame after shifting MODULE_001+002 +21 studs in X; house left plane becomes X=24.

level_model.note: Z values are constructive prototype quantization, not survey measurements. Altitude is conserved by the two ascending runs.

unresolved: Exact real tread count, riser height and tread depth.
Exact dimensions of the turning landing.
Exact full depth/shape of the covered lower void beyond the directly constrained open bay.
Exact plan span and step geometry of the future timber-deck connection.
Final LEGO connection detail between MODULE 003 and MODULE 001.

prototype_quantization.rationale: Coarse monotone LEGO raster preserves start, turn, total rise and platform arrival without claiming actual stair-step metrics.

human_gate_correction_042.current_overlap_cause: No literal XY solid intersection with the host: the stair is already outside the house in X. The local visual error comes from the upper run occupying Y62..75 while the host depth extends to rear plane Y72, so Y62..72 shares ten studs of house-depth projection.
photo_evidence_for_rearward_offset: P3 keeps the stair/masonry circulation visibly outside the principal house mass.
P4 places the masonry complex at the rear-side zone and shows the stair wrapping outside it rather than disappearing into the body.
P5 recuts the stair from the rear-side angle and is consistent with the circulation sitting farther rearward than the 041 placement.
human_gate_correction_042.human_constraint: The real stair remains entirely outside the house footprint at the wall and is slightly farther rearward; this is qualitative and does not provide a metric.

correction.derivation: Minimum integer shift that moves the nearest upper-run coordinate from Y62 to host rear plane Y72; no extra offset is claimed.
Minimum integer translation that moves upper stair envelope X7..15 to X16..24, touching but not crossing house wall plane X24.

obstructing_rail.reason: After stair +9 X, this local rear platform parapet lies directly across the high stair/platform circulation opening.

correction_1_platform_edge.human_declared_relation: The exposed platform edge beside the stair arrival requires fall protection while the stair opening remains passable.
photo_confirmed_geometry: P3 shows a protected masonry edge adjacent to the stair/platform zone rather than an unrestricted drop.
P4/P5 keep the stair arrival distinct from the protected outer platform edge.

constructive_approximation.note: Coordinates are LEGO constructive quantization; no metric dimension is inferred from the human markup.

correction_2_lower_openings.human_declared_relation: The visually false lower opening must be closed and the human-marked real lower opening must remain/open in the correct face.
photo_confirmed_geometry: P4 and P5 directly show the large real rectangular opening on the rear face below the masonry platform.
P2/P3 do not support a second through-opening on the opposite/front lower face.

constructive_approximation.note: The void principle remains; only its visible face distribution is corrected.

correction_3_smooth_parapets.human_declared_relation: Stair parapets have a smooth, continuous upper silhouette rather than a crenellated sequence of brick tops.
photo_confirmed_geometry: P3 and especially P5 show continuous sloping masonry parapet tops along the stair runs.

constructive_approximation.method: placement-approved BRICK_SLOPED_45_2X1 cap courses over the existing parapet bodies
constructive_approximation.preserves: all tread, stringer, run and level coordinates
constructive_approximation.note: Shape proxy only; this mission does not generalize the technique or optimize piece selection.

correction_4_wall_continuity.human_declared_relation: The house-side/left stair parapet must continue the wall plane rather than begin after a visible offset.
photo_confirmed_geometry: P5 shows the upper stair parapet joining the adjacent wall line without a detached lateral gap.

constructive_approximation.relation: column outer face X24 is flush with host wall plane; existing upper parapet continues at X23/Y72
